governed_construct: An `if` statement located inside a function body (function declaration, function expression, arrow function, method, constructor, accessor). `if` statements at module top level are not instances.
interpretation: The rule asks that conditional logic inside functions be flattened with early exits (return, throw, continue, break) instead of nesting conditions. Operationally, an `if` statement is non-conforming when it is a descendant of the consequent or alternate branch of another `if` statement within the same function, at any depth (including through intervening loops, blocks, try/catch/finally, or switch), without crossing a nested function boundary; an `if` inside a nested function or callback is judged only against `if` statements of that inner function. An `else if` chain is flat, not nested: an IfStatement that is directly the alternate of another IfStatement does not count as nested in it (but an `if` inside the blocks of an else-if branch, or inside a plain `else { ... }` block, does). Guard clauses, sequential ifs, else-if chains and ifs inside loops that are not themselves inside an `if` all conform. Ternaries, logical-operator short-circuits and switch statements are not governed instances. A file with no `if` statement inside any function is NOT_APPLICABLE. Mentions of `if` in comments or strings are irrelevant.
